key_insight: Visual attribution methods commonly used to explain LVLM outputs for chest X-rays often do not faithfully reflect the actual visual evidence the model relied on; the paper introduces a rigorous evaluation approach to test and quantify attribution faithfulness.
problem_solved: Provides a principled way to verify whether visual explanations (e.g., saliency maps, heatmaps) for LVLM chest X-ray reasoning truly correspond to the model's visual evidence, addressing a critical trust and safety gap for clinical use.
method: Design a task-specific evaluation framework that tests attribution faithfulness using interventions, counterfactuals, and (when available) region-level annotations.
Systematically benchmark popular attribution techniques on chest X-ray reasoning tasks to identify which methods are faithful versus spurious.
Define metrics and recommended best practices to assess and improve visual attribution reliability for LVLMs in medical imaging.
impact: Helps AI/ML practitioners and clinicians audit and trust LVLM explanations by providing concrete tests and metrics for visual grounding, reducing the risk of deploying models with misleading attributions in clinical settings.
visual_elements: Flowchart of the evaluation pipeline: X-ray input → LVLM prediction → attribution map → intervention/counterfactual → faithfulness score
Side-by-side chest X-ray examples showing faithful vs. spurious attribution heatmaps
Bar chart comparing multiple attribution methods across the proposed faithfulness metrics
Checklist-style infographic summarizing recommended practices for attribution evaluation and deployment
paper_title: Rethinking Visual Attribution for Chest X-ray Reasoning in Large Vision Language Models
paper_authors: Guangzhi Xiong, Qiao Jin, Sanchit Sinha, Zhiyong Lu, Aidong Zhang
